analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/hardware-support.md: it bumps the "Last updated" date and adds a head-side paragraph (lines 371-408) describing selected-model recovery. I examined the base excerpt (453-843) and the head excerpt (1-445), which includes the new paragraph. No code, protocol, key, attestation, cache-format or authorization behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

The documented behavior is a capacity-tick recovery loop in ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift. It retries operator-selected models that memory kept out. It loads with allowEviction:false. It may unload only idle resident models that have no evictionExclusions entry and are not protected by isProtectedFromRecoveryEviction. It honors Autopilot dwell, lease and idle rules, and rechecks each victim right before unload. It still goes through the same load gate: the pending-load claim, the post-load KV headroom probe and Super's LOAD-claim room. Relevant threat IDs are T-016 and T-029 (availability) and A-018 (serving availability). The text claims no new trust boundary crossing, no new wire fields and no change to TB-002, TB-011 or TB-012.

Open questions for deeper review, none a finding here. I did not see the Swift source, so I cannot confirm that it matches the documented guards. I cannot confirm that the victim eviction respects the add-on hold in TB-012, since the doc lists evictionExclusions but does not name add-on holds explicitly. I also cannot confirm that recovery's pre-load eviction cannot be driven by a local or remote party to churn residency (an availability concern only). The doc says victims are evicted before the load's own checks, so a load failing for another reason still costs one attempt's evictions; this is bounded, because that failure ends recovery for the model. The patch excerpt is truncated, but the head text shows the full new paragraph. The base side shows no related content.

No security regression or invalidated threat-model assumption was identified from documentation alone.
